i18n.en: He perfected the rites and the august divine offices.
i18n._note_alt: Or: 'He set in (his) hand the august rites and divine functions.'

lines.commentary: *ĝarza me maḫ šu mi-ni-ib-šu-du7* — *he perfected the rites and the august divine offices*. The line deploys the Sumerian creation-summary formula: a divine actor *perfects* (verbal-phrase *šu šu-du7* 'sets-in-hand to-complete') the *ĝarza* (rites) and the *me* (the Sumerian flagship-untranslatable theological-keyword for **divine-offices / cosmic-functions**; covered by the central entry `me-sumerian-divine-offices-cosmic-functions`). The subject is implicit (probably An or Enki). The line recurs at FLS-WOH-B:8 as the closing-of-the-kingship-descent pericope. An alternative more-literal rendering — *he set in (his) hand the august rites and divine functions* — is preserved in the source `_note_alt` field.

i18n.en: He commanded water for the land, saying: I will establish well-being there.

lines.commentary: *ki a im-ma-ab-dug4 silim ga-mu-ni-in-ĝar* — *he commanded water for the land, saying: I will establish well-being there*. The line closes the divine-speaker's resolution-sequence by binding the **water-allotment** to the **well-being-establishment**: water is commanded for the land precisely so that *silim* 'well-being / health / soundness' can be established. The Sumerian *silim* (Akkadian-loanword *šalāmu* 'to be well') is the broad-eudaimonia-vocabulary; cognate with Hebrew *shalom* (West-Semitic; the cognate is direct via Akkadian intermediate).

i18n.en: An, Enlil, Enki, and Ninhursaĝa —

lines.commentary: **The divine quartet** — An, Enlil, Enki, Ninḫursaĝa. The standard Sumerian senior-divine-cluster (the cosmic-triad An / Enlil / Enki plus the birth-goddess Ninḫursaĝa). This is the **flood-decision council** in the Mesopotamian flood-tradition; the same four gods preside at Atrahasis I.i.6-15 and Gilgamesh XI.14-19. The new central entry `an-enlil-enki-ninhursaga-flood-council-quartet-cross-corpus` houses the quartet specifically; the existing central entry `an-enlil-nudimmud-cosmic-triad-cross-corpus` houses the triad (An-Enlil-Nudimmud / Enki) in general-cosmic-function contexts. The Hebrew flood-narrative collapses the divine-quartet into the singular-deity YHWH; the Mesopotamian-Hebrew shift is documented at the new central entry's rationale.

i18n.en: when they had fashioned the black-headed people,

lines.commentary: *saĝ gig2-ga* — *the black-headed (people)*. The standard Sumerian self-designation for **humans / the Sumerian-Akkadian population**; the lexeme is corpus-wide across Sumerian literature (the Sumerian King List, Gudea Cylinders, Enki and the World Order, Inana's Descent) and corpus-wide across Akkadian literature (Atrahasis, Enuma Elish, Gilgamesh — under the Akkadian-cognate *ṣalmāt qaqqadi*). The new central entry `sag-gig-ga-black-headed-people-sumerian-self-designation-cross-corpus` houses the lexeme as the concrete-ethnonymic-counterpart to the abstract-collective `nam-lu2-ulu3-sumerian-humankind-cross-corpus`. The Hebrew comparandum is *bnei Adam* — patronymic rather than ethnonymic.

i18n.en: the small animals multiplied from the ground in every place,

lines.commentary: *niĝ2-gilim ki-ta ki-ta mu-lu-lu* — *the small animals multiplied from the ground in every place*. The line opens the creation-of-animals sequence at A:13-14 (Sumerian parallel to Gen 1:24-25). The verb *lu* 'to be abundant / multiply' is iterated-and-reduplicated for intensified-aspect: the animals multiply abundantly from every locality. The *niĝ2-gilim* small-animal-class noun is the broad-category for terrestrial small-fauna; covered in the Enki and Ninmaḫ overlay glossary.

i18n.en: and the herd-beasts, the four-legged creatures, were set as fitting ornament of the open country.

lines.commentary: *maš2-anše niĝ2-ur2-4 edin-na me-te-a-aš bi2-ib2-ĝal2* — *and the herd-beasts, the four-legged creatures, were set as fitting ornament of the open country*. The line completes the creation-of-animals sequence. The Sumerian *me-te* 'fitting ornament / proper attribute / decorum' (overlay entry `me-te-edin-fitting-attribute-of-open-country`) is the **aesthetic-cosmological** category — the world adorned with its proper inhabitants. The Hebrew Bible parallel is the *tov / tov me'od* declarations of Gen 1 (each day's creation pronounced *good / very good*); a comparative-mythology link of the *fittingness-aesthetic-cosmology* type.

i18n.en: [Approximately 32 lines missing.]

lines.commentary: Reduced to a single preserved verbal-prefix *mu-un-*. The line is unrecoverable; only the cuneiform sign-residue confirms continued narrative-action by an animate subject.
Reduced to the unparsed sign-cluster *AM3*. The line is unrecoverable beyond confirming residual cuneiform-sign-presence.

i18n.en: […] I will give counsel […]

lines.commentary: *X de5-ga ga-ba-ni-in-X* — *I will give counsel*. The preserved verb *de5* 'to collect / gather / take-counsel' (in the imperfective *ga-ba-* future-cohortative) signals a first-person divine speaker resolving to give counsel; the addressee is unrecoverable. The line plausibly opens the segment-B section in which the divine speaker plans the city-foundation arrangements (B:4-10).

i18n.en: Let me cause their toil to be relieved before (my) eyes […]

lines.commentary: *[du]-lum-bi igi ga-ba-ni-ib-du8-du8-X* — *Let me cause their toil to be relieved before (my) eyes*. The line is a parallel-passage to the Atrahasis I.i divine-toil pericope; the *du-lum* / Akkadian-loanword *dullu* is the cross-corpus divine-toil-keyword covered by the existing central entry `du-lum-dullu-divine-toil-relieved-by-humans-cross-corpus`. The verb *du8* 'to spread / relieve / release' indicates the toil is to be **relieved** — the standard Mesopotamian *humans-relieve-divine-toil* theology; the divine speaker plans to alleviate the gods' burden through the institution-of-humans.

i18n.en: […] Let the builder of the Land dig (its) firm foundation.

lines.commentary: *X šidim kalam-ma-ke4 uš gen6 ḫa-ba-ab-ba-al* — *let the builder of the Land dig (its) firm foundation*. The line names the *šidim* 'builder' (the Sumerian construction-foreman / architect; Akkadian-loanword *šitimgallu* / *šitimmu*) as the city-and-foundation-laying agent. The *kalam* 'Land' is the Sumerian collective-territorial-identity (covered by the existing central entry `kalam-ka-na-ag-the-land-cross-corpus`). The line transitions from divine-speech to the human / institutional construction-implementation.

i18n.en: [When …] when kingship had descended from heaven,

lines.commentary: ***nam-lugal an-ta ed3-de3-a-ba* — *when kingship had descended from heaven*.** **THE foundational Sumerian antediluvian-kingship formula** — the opening of the Sumerian King List (ETCSL 2.1.1) and the keynote of the Mesopotamian primordial-kingship-tradition. Covered by the new central entry `nam-lugal-an-ta-ed-de-a-ba-kingship-descended-from-heaven-cross-corpus`. The formula recurs at FLS-WOH-B:7 immediately (the regalia-couplet *men-gu-za* — crown-and-throne — descending alongside kingship). The Hebrew Bible's kingship-from-divine-source theology (Exod 15:18, *malkhut shamayim*, the *covenanted-kingship* concept) is functional-parallel rather than philologically-cognate.

i18n.en: when the august crown and the throne of kingship had descended from heaven,

lines.commentary: *men maḫ ^ĝišgu-za nam-lugal-la an-ta ed3-a-ba* — *when the august crown and the throne of kingship had descended from heaven*. The regalia-couplet — *men* 'crown' + *gu-za* 'throne' — are the synecdochic-regalia of the descended-kingship; the same pairing is the canonical Sumerian-Akkadian royal-iconography. The Hebrew comparandum is *keter* 'crown' + *kisse melekh* 'throne of the kingdom' (Esth, 1-2 Kgs); the comparative-mythology link is documented at the overlay entry `men-gu-za-nam-lugal-crown-and-throne-of-kingship-regalia-formula`.

i18n.en: he perfected the [rites and] august [divine offices].

lines.commentary: *[ĝarza me] maḫ šu mi-ni-ib-šu-du7* — *he perfected the [rites and] august [divine offices]*. The line recurs the creation-summary formula of FLS-WOH-A:9, here applied to the kingship-and-regalia descent of vv 6-7: kingship descends; the august-rites-and-divine-offices are perfected (i.e. instituted in their proper-functional-arrangement). The *me* divine-offices-and-cosmic-functions lexeme is covered by the existing central entry `me-sumerian-divine-offices-cosmic-functions`.

i18n.en: [For those cities the bricks were] cast on holy ground.

lines.commentary: *[iri-bi-e]-ne [šeg12-bi ki kug-ga im]-ma-an-da-šub* — *for those cities the bricks were cast on holy ground*. The line opens the five-antediluvian-cities pericope (B:9-16) by re-deploying the *brick-cast-on-holy-ground* formula of FLS-WOH-A:6 — establishing the antediluvian-cities as ritually-grounded foundations. The brick-cast inclusio is the structural-frame for the five-cities-and-five-founder-divinities listing at B:11-15.

i18n.en: Their names were called out and they were assigned by gauged measure.

lines.commentary: *mu-bi ba-an-sa4 kab dug4-ga ba-ḫal-ḫal-la* — *their names were called out and they were assigned by gauged measure*. The line is the **opening of the city-foundation inclusio** (closed at FLS-WOH-B:16). The Sumerian *kab dug-ga* 'gauged-measure-declaration' + *ba-ḫal-ḫal-la* 'they were distributed by allotment' is the administrative-juridical idiom for **formal-divine-allotment-by-quantified-measure**. Covered by the overlay entry `kab-dug-ga-ba-hal-hal-la-allotment-by-gauged-measure-city-founding-formula`. The Hebrew comparandum is the *goral* 'lot' and *cheleq* 'portion' divine-allotment vocabulary (Deut 32:8-9).

i18n.en: The first of these cities, Eridug, he gave to Nudimmud the leader.

lines.commentary: **The first antediluvian city — Eridug, given to Nudimmud (Enki).** *nesaĝ* 'first-fruit-offering' opens the list (the first city is the *first-offering* of the city-foundation sequence). **Eridug** (Akkadian Eridu; modern Tell Abu Shahrein) is the southernmost Sumerian city and traditionally the *first* city of the Sumerian world; Nudimmud (the Enki-fashioner-epithet, covered by the existing central entry `an-enlil-nudimmud-cosmic-triad-cross-corpus`) is its tutelary deity. The five-antediluvian-cities pentad is covered by the new central entry `five-antediluvian-cities-eridug-bad-tibira-larag-zimbir-shuruppag-cross-corpus`; cross-corpus to the Sumerian King List antediluvian-section, the Berossus-tradition, and the Apkallu-tradition.

i18n.en: The second, Bad-tibira, he gave to the high-status woman.

lines.commentary: **The second antediluvian city — Bad-tibira, given to the *nu-gig* (high-status / sacred-class woman).** The *nu-gig* is **anonymous** — designated by class-noun rather than proper-name; she is most-plausibly **Inana** under her *nu-gig*-epithet (Bad-tibira had a major Inana-cult). The deliberate epithet-rather-than-name parallels Eridug-Nudimmud (Enki as fashioner) — both founder-divinities are designated by office / epithet rather than standard-cult-name. The *nu-gig* lexeme is covered by the new central entry `nu-gig-high-status-woman-sacred-class-cross-corpus` which sits in cross-corpus sibling-cluster with the Hebrew *qedeshah* and *zonah* class-terms; the modern-scholarly deprecation of the older 'sacred prostitute' translation is documented in the entry.

i18n.en: The third, Larag, he gave to Pabilsaĝ.

lines.commentary: **The third antediluvian city — Larag, given to Pabilsaĝ.** Pabilsaĝ is a relatively-obscure Sumerian deity, associated with Larag and with the late-Mesopotamian astronomical zodiacal-Sagittarius (Akkadian *pa-bil-sag-ga* / Greek *Toxotēs*); see the overlay entry `pabilsag-bowman-deity-larag-founder-divinity`. The ETCSL form *^dpa-bil2-«ḫur»-saĝ* contains the editorial-emendation marker «ḫur» (the manuscript reads *ḫur*; the editor regards it as scribal-error and prefers *pa-bil2-saĝ*); per the project-wide overlay convention `manuscript-variant-inline-rendering-convention` the variant is silently collapsed in the English prose.

i18n.en: The fourth, Zimbir, he gave to the young hero Utu.

lines.commentary: **The fourth antediluvian city — Zimbir (Akkadian Sippar), given to Utu (Akkadian Šamaš), the young hero.** Zimbir was the cult-center of the sun-god Utu / Šamaš; the city is famous in modern scholarship under its Akkadian-form Sippar (modern Tell Abu Habbah). The new central entry `utu-shamash-sun-god-justice-divinity-cross-corpus` houses the deity with cross-corpus comparanda (Akkadian Šamaš, Hebrew *shemesh*, the *Beit Shemesh* cult-name). The Sumerian-source form *Zimbir* is preserved per the project-wide overlay convention `sumerian-proper-name-transliteration-convention`.

i18n.en: The fifth, Šuruppag, he gave to Sud.

lines.commentary: **The fifth and final antediluvian city — Šuruppag, given to Sud.** Šuruppag (Akkadian Shuruppak; modern Tell Fara) is the **home-city of Ziusudra** (the flood-survivor); cross-corpus to Gilgamesh XI.11 (*Šuruppak*) and the Sumerian Instructions of Shuruppak (ETCSL 5.6.1). The founder-deity Sud is the pre-Ninlil name of Enlil's spouse (Enlil-and-Sud myth ETCSL 1.2.2 narrates the courtship and the name-change). See the overlay entry `shuruppag-ziusudras-city`.

lines.translit: iri-be2-e-ne mu-bi ba-an-sa4-a kab dug4-ga ba-ḫal-ḫal-la

i18n.en: These cities — their names had been called out, they had been assigned by gauged measure.

lines.commentary: *iri-be2-e-ne mu-bi ba-an-sa4-a kab dug4-ga ba-ḫal-ḫal-la* — *these cities — their names had been called out, they had been assigned by gauged measure*. The inclusio closes the city-foundation pericope by recurring the formula of FLS-WOH-B:10 in the perfective. See the overlay entry `kab-dug-ga-ba-hal-hal-la-allotment-by-gauged-measure-city-founding-formula`.
lines.cuneiform: 𒌷𒁉𒂊𒉈 𒈬𒁉 𒁀𒀭𒄷𒈿𒀀 𒆏 𒅗𒂵 𒁀𒆷

lines.translit: id2 IM GUN2^? ma-an-šu4-am3 im-ma-al-la a im-ma-an-de6

i18n.en: The watercourse […] was covered for them; […] carried the water.

lines.commentary: *id2 IM GUN2^? ma-an-šu4-am3 im-ma-al-la a im-ma-an-de6* — partially-obscure; ETCSL preserves *IM*, *GUN2^?*, and the *im-ma-al-la* as unparsed sign-clusters with philological-uncertainty markers. The preserved continuation *a im-ma-an-de6* — *(the) water was carried* — names the **water-allocation** moment in the post-city-founding institution of the watercourse-system. The line plausibly continues the divine-water-allotment sequence of FLS-WOH-A:10.
lines.cuneiform: 𒀀𒇉 𒅎  𒈠𒀭𒌋𒀀𒀭 𒅎𒈠𒀠𒆷 𒀀 𒅎𒈠𒀭𒁺

lines.translit: id2 tur-tur-re šu luḫ-bi ĜAR ḪAR-ḪAR mi-ni-ib2-ĝar-ĝar

i18n.en: Of the smaller watercourses, their cleansing-channels […] were set in place.

lines.commentary: *id2 tur-tur-re šu luḫ-bi ĜAR ḪAR-ḪAR mi-ni-ib2-ĝar-ĝar* — *of the smaller watercourses, their cleansing-channels were set in place*. The line completes the water-allocation institution at B:17-18: the major watercourses (*id2*, B:17) are allocated; the minor cleansing-channels (*id2 tur-tur*, B:18) are likewise set up. The Sumerian *šu luḫ* 'cleansing / purification' is the technical-irrigation-and-temple-purification vocabulary.

i18n.en: [Approximately 34 lines missing.]
The dwelling-place of heaven […]

lines.commentary: *ki-tuš an-na X ...* — *the dwelling-place of heaven ...*. The line opens segment C (after the ~34-line lacuna) with a reference to the **dwelling-place of heaven** (*ki-tuš an-na* — the cosmic-residence of An / the celestial realm). The continuation is bracketed.
Reduced to *e-...* — a single preserved verbal-prefix or noun-fragment. Unrecoverable.

i18n.en: The flood […]

lines.commentary: ***a-ma-ru ...* — *the flood ...***. The first explicit mention of the flood in the preserved-text. The Sumerian *a-ma-ru* — the textual-keyword of this composition and the foundational Sumerian flood-vocabulary lexeme — is covered by the new central entry `a-ma-ru-abubu-mabbul-great-flood-vocabulary-cross-corpus`. The lexeme sits in cross-corpus three-way sibling-cluster with the Akkadian *abūbu* (Atrahasis / Gilgamesh XI) and the Hebrew *mabbul* (Gen 6-11). The line's continuation is bracketed; the announcement of the flood is fully-developed at FLS-WOH-C:22-26.

i18n.en: Humankind […]

lines.commentary: *nam-lu2-[ulu3 ...]* — *humankind ...*. Only the abstract-collective *nam-lu2-ulu3* (covered by the existing central entry `nam-lu2-ulu3-sumerian-humankind-cross-corpus`) is preserved; the continuation is bracketed. The line plausibly begins the description of humankind's-impending-fate after the flood-announcement at C:3.

i18n.en: Thus it was done […]

lines.commentary: *ur5-gin7 bi2-in-ak ...* — *thus it was done ...*. The Sumerian demonstrative-equative *ur5-gin7* 'in this manner / thus' + the perfective *bi2-in-ak* 'he / they did' is a narrative-summary formula. The continuation is bracketed.

i18n.en: In those days Nintur […] fashioned […]

lines.commentary: *ud-bi-a ^dnin-tur5 ... DIM2 A ...* — *In those days Nintur ... fashioned ...*. The temporal-deictic *ud-bi-a* 'in those days' opens a narrative-flashback or reorienting-temporal frame. **Nintur** (the birth-goddess; covered by the new central entry `nintur-nintud-ninhursaga-birth-goddess-epithet-cluster-cross-corpus`) is the subject of the *dim2* 'to fashion / create' verb (preserved as the upper-case unparsed *DIM2*). The line is fragmentary but signals Nintur's role as the **fashioner of (humankind / creatures)** — paralleling the Enki and Ninmaḫ creation-of-humans pericope.

i18n.en: Holy Inana was setting up a lament for her people.

lines.commentary: *kug ^dinana-ke4 uĝ3-bi-še3 a-nir mu-[un-ĝa2-ĝa2]* — *Holy Inana was setting up a lament for her people*. The line places Inana (Akkadian Ishtar) as the **divine-feminine lament-figure** in the face of the coming flood. Covered by the new central entry `inana-laments-her-people-flood-divine-feminine-lament-cross-corpus`. The Sumerian city-lament tradition (ETCSL 2.2.x — the Lament for Ur, Lament for Sumer and Ur, Eridu Lament) develops the divine-feminine-lament genre extensively; the Hebrew structural-parallel is the Rachel-weeping-for-her-children at Jer 31:15 (covered by the existing central entry `havah-li-banim-rachel-cry`).

i18n.en: Enki took counsel in his own heart.

lines.commentary: ***Enki šag4 ni2-te-na-ke4 ad i-ni-in-gi4-gi4* — *Enki took counsel in his own heart***. The foundational **Enki-private-deliberation** trope: the wisdom-god, alone, considering the divine flood-decree. Covered by the new central entry `enki-deliberates-in-his-own-heart-wisdom-god-private-deliberation-cross-corpus`. The Hebrew structural-parallels are Yahweh's pre-flood deliberation at Gen 6:6 (*va-yit'atzev el libbo* — *and he grieved to his heart*) and Yahweh's pre-Sodom deliberation at Gen 18:17 (*ha-mekhasse ani me-Avraham asher ani oseh* — *shall I hide from Abraham what I am doing?*).

i18n.en: An, Enlil, Enki, and Ninhursaĝa —

lines.commentary: The divine quartet — An, Enlil, Enki, Ninḫursaĝa — recurs (cf. FLS-WOH-A:11) in the flood-council context. See the new central entry `an-enlil-enki-ninhursaga-flood-council-quartet-cross-corpus`.

lines.translit: diĝir an ki-ke4 mu an ^den-lil2 mu-X-[pad3]

i18n.en: the gods of heaven and earth invoked the names of An and Enlil.

lines.commentary: *diĝir an ki-ke4 mu an ^den-lil2 mu-X-[pad3]* — *the gods of heaven and earth invoked the names of An and Enlil*. The verb *pad3* 'to find / invoke (a name in an oath)' is the standard Sumerian oath-invocation idiom; the line foreshadows the *zi an-na zi ki-a i3-pad3-de3* oath-formula at FLS-WOH-E:1-2 (covered by the new central entry `zi-an-na-zi-ki-a-nish-ilim-oath-by-life-of-heaven-and-earth-cross-corpus`). The deities here perform the **assembly-oath** that binds the flood-decree as irrevocable (covered by the new central entry `di-til-la-puhrum-irrevocability-of-divine-assembly-decree-cross-corpus`).
lines.cuneiform: 𒀭 𒀭 𒆠𒆤 𒈬 𒀭 𒀭𒂗𒆤 𒈬𒅆𒊒

i18n.en: In those days Ziusudra the king, the gudug-priest, […]

lines.commentary: **Ziusudra's introduction in the preserved text** — *ud-ba zi-ud-su3-ra2 lugal-am3 gudug X ...* — *In those days Ziusudra was the king, the gudug-priest, ...*. Ziusudra's name parses transparently in Sumerian as *zi* 'life-breath' + *ud* 'day' + *su3-ra2* 'long, distant' — *life of long days*. The name is **proleptic**: it encodes the protagonist's eventual apotheosis (FLS-WOH-E:7-8 — *til3 diĝir-gin7* 'life like a god'; *zi da-ri2 diĝir-gin7* 'eternal life like a god'). Covered by the new central entry `ziusudra-atrahasis-utnapishtim-noach-flood-survivor-name-cluster-cross-corpus` — the five-tradition cross-corpus sibling-cluster (Sumerian Ziusudra / Akkadian Atra-ḫasīs / Akkadian Ūta-napishtim / Greek Xisouthros / Hebrew Noach). The line also gives Ziusudra two titles: *lugal* 'the king' and *gudug* (a specific Mesopotamian priestly-office; covered by the overlay entry `gudug-priest-mesopotamian-temple-office`). The priest-king dual-office parallels the Hebrew Melchizedek (Gen 14:18-20).

i18n.en: He fashioned a […], turning (his) head (towards) heaven […]

lines.commentary: *an saĝ NIĜIN mu-un-dim2-dim2 EN ...* — *He fashioned a ..., turning (his) head (towards) heaven ...*. The unparsed *NIĜIN* and *EN* sign-clusters preserve philological-uncertainty in the cuneiform-reading. The preserved-fragment indicates Ziusudra's **head-turned-towards-heaven** posture — a ritual / supplicatory gesture preceding the revelation-of-the-flood-warning.

i18n.en: In humility, placing his words, drawing near in awe […]

lines.commentary: *nam-sun5-na inim sig10-sig10-ge ni2 teĝ3-ĝe26 ...* — *in humility, placing his words, drawing near in awe ...*. The *nam-sun5-na* 'humility' + *ni2 teĝ3* 'to draw near in awe / fear' construction is the Sumerian **reverent-supplication** formula. Ziusudra's day-by-day standing-attendance posture (continued at C:14) is the **wakeful-vigilant-supplication** preceding the revelation.

i18n.en: Day after day, standing in steady attendance […]

lines.commentary: *ud šu2-uš-e saĝ us2 gub-ba ...* — *day after day, standing in steady attendance ...*. The *ud šu2-uš-e* 'day-after-day / continuously' + *saĝ us2 gub-ba* 'standing with head adjacent / in steady attendance' continues the day-by-day-vigilance posture of C:13. The line sets up the **revelation-by-waking-utterance** at C:15.

i18n.en: Something that was not a dream came forth, an utterance […]

lines.commentary: ***ma-mu2 nu-me-a ed2-de3 inim /bal\ ...* — *something that was not a dream came forth, an utterance ...***. The **waking-revelation / not-a-dream** trope: Enki communicates to Ziusudra not through a dream but through an **audible-utterance** that the text explicitly distinguishes from dream-revelation by negation. Covered by the new central entry `ma-mu-nu-me-a-not-a-dream-waking-revelation-cross-corpus`. The Hebrew structural-parallel is Num 12:6-8 (the dream-vs-mouth-to-mouth distinction in Yahweh's prophetic-revelation hierarchy).

i18n.en: Invoking by name (the gods of) heaven and earth […]

lines.commentary: *mu an ki-bi-ta pad3-pad3-de3 ...* — *invoking by name (the gods of) heaven and earth ...*. The verb *pad3* 'to invoke (a name in an oath)' is reduplicated for iterative-aspect; the line continues the oath-and-invocation pattern of C:10 and foreshadows the FLS-WOH-E:1-2 oath-by-the-life-of-heaven-and-earth.

i18n.en: Toward the Ki-ur the gods (made) a wall […]

lines.commentary: *ki-ur3-še3 diĝir-re-e-ne e2-ĝar8 ...* — *toward the Ki-ur the gods (made) a wall ...*. The **Ki-ur** is the courtyard / cult-precinct of the E-kur temple of Enlil at Nippur — Enlil's principal cult-center (the E-kur is covered by the existing central entry `ekur-house-of-the-mountain-enlil-temple-cross-corpus`). The *e2-ĝar8* 'wall' here is the **wall through which Enki speaks** — anticipating the wall-side-wall trope at FLS-WOH-C:19-21.

i18n.en: Ziusudra, standing alongside, gave ear (to it).

lines.commentary: *zi-ud-su3-ra2 da-bi gub-ba ĝiš mu-[un-tuku]* — *Ziusudra, standing alongside, gave ear (to it)*. The Sumerian idiom *ĝiš tuku* (literally 'to have ear / wood') is the standard 'to hear / attend to' idiom; the construction *da-bi gub-ba* 'standing at the side' positions Ziusudra at the side-wall — the geometry of the through-the-wall-revelation.

i18n.en: (He said:) 'Side-wall, stand at my left side […]'

lines.commentary: ***iz-zi-da a2 gab2-bu-ĝu10 gub-ba ...* — *(He said:) 'Side-wall, stand at my left side ...'***. The **talking-through-the-wall trope** — Enki addresses not Ziusudra directly but the side-wall, so as not-technically-violate the oath-of-silence. Covered by the new central entry `iz-zi-da-kikkish-talking-through-the-wall-to-keep-an-oath-flood-trope-cross-corpus`. The cross-corpus Akkadian parallel is Gilgamesh XI.21-22 (*kikkiš kikkiš igâru igâru* — *reed-hut, reed-hut! wall, wall!*); Atrahasis III.i.20 deploys the same trope. The Hebrew flood-narrative has no exact parallel; the Yahweh-singular-decision has dispensed with the assembly-oath that motivates the wall-trope.

i18n.en: 'Side-wall, I will speak a word to you; let [my] word [be heeded].'

lines.commentary: *iz-zi-da inim ga-ra-ab-dug4 inim-[ĝu10 ḫe2-dab5]* — *'Side-wall, I will speak a word to you; let [my] word [be heeded]'*. The reduplicated address-to-the-wall continues from C:19; the construction *inim dug4* + *inim dab5* 'to speak a word / let the word be seized' frames the address as binding-instruction (the wall is to retain Enki's word for the listening-Ziusudra).

i18n.en: '[Let attention be paid] to my counsel.'

lines.commentary: *na de5-ga-ĝu10 ĝizzal [ḫe2-em-ši-ak]* — *'[Let attention be paid] to my counsel'*. The Sumerian *na de5* 'counsel / advice' + *ĝizzal ak* 'to give ear / attend' is the standard wisdom-literature attention-formula (parallels in the Instructions of Shuruppak ETCSL 5.6.1 — addressed *from* Šuruppak *to* Ziusudra in the wisdom-tradition).

i18n.en: 'By our […], a flood will sweep over the cult-centres […]'

lines.commentary: ***DAG-me-a a-ma-ru ugu kab dug4-[ga ...] ba-/ur3\ ...* — *'By our [...], a flood will sweep over the cult-centres ...'***. The **explicit announcement of the coming flood**. The opening *DAG-me-a* is partially-obscure (the *DAG* sign has multiple values; ETCSL preserves the sign-uppercase to flag the philological-crux); the most-plausible parsing is *dag-me-a* 'in our cult-stations / dwelling-places' — the divine collective's seats. See the overlay entry `dag-me-a-our-dwelling-places-c22-crux`. The continuation *ugu kab dug4-ga ba-ur3* — *will sweep over the cult-centres / the gauged-places* — recurs verbatim at FLS-WOH-D:2 as the actualization. The destruction-decree cluster is covered by the new central entry `divine-decree-to-destroy-humankind-flood-trope-cross-corpus`; cross-corpus Atrahasis II.viii, Gilgamesh XI.14, Hebrew Gen 6:5-7.
lines.cuneiform: 𒁖𒈨𒀀 𒀀𒈠𒊒 𒌋𒅗 𒆏 𒅗𒂵  𒁀𒃡

i18n.en: 'To destroy the seed of humankind — [such has been its destiny decreed].'

lines.commentary: ***numun nam-lu2-ulu3 ḫa-lam-e-de3 [nam-bi ba-tar]* — *'To destroy the seed of humankind — [such has been its destiny decreed]'***. The explicit destruction-decree. The verbal *nam tar* 'to cut a destiny' (covered by the existing central entry `nam-sumerian-destiny-fate-cross-corpus`) is here applied to the **destruction-of-the-seed-of-humankind** (covered by the overlay entry `numun-nam-lu-ulu-seed-of-humankind-c23` and the new central entry `divine-decree-to-destroy-humankind-flood-trope-cross-corpus`). Cross-corpus Atrahasis II.viii, Gilgamesh XI.14, Hebrew Gen 6:7 (*emcheh et ha-adam* — *I will blot out humankind*). The structural-counterpart is Ziusudra's preservation-of-the-seed at FLS-WOH-E:10.

lines.translit: di-til-la inim pu-uḫ2-ru-[um-ma-ka šu gi4-gi4 nu-ĝal2]

i18n.en: 'It is a concluded verdict; the word of the [assembly cannot be revoked].'

lines.commentary: ***di-til-la inim pu-uḫ2-ru-[um-ma-ka šu gi4-gi4 nu-ĝal2]* — *'It is a concluded verdict; the word of the [assembly cannot be revoked]'***. The foundational Sumerian **irrevocability-of-divine-decree** formula. The technical-juridical *di-til-la* 'completed-court-case' + *pu-uḫ2-ru-um* 'assembly' (the Sumerian-Akkadian *puḫrum*) + *šu gi4-gi4 nu-ĝal2* 'no returning the hand' (= no revocation). Covered by the new central entry `di-til-la-puhrum-irrevocability-of-divine-assembly-decree-cross-corpus`. The Hebrew structural-parallel is *sod YHWH* (Jer 23:18; Ps 89:8) and the irrevocability-of-YHWH's-plan (Isa 14:24-27; 46:10-11).
lines.cuneiform: 𒁲𒌀𒆷 𒅗 𒁍𒊒𒌝𒈠𒅗 𒋗 𒄄𒄄 𒉡𒅅

i18n.en: 'The command spoken by An and En[lil] [cannot be overturned].'

lines.commentary: *inim dug4-ga an ^den-[lil2-la2-ka] [šu bal-e nu-zu]* — *'The command spoken by An and En[lil] [cannot be overturned]'*. The line restates the irrevocability-of-the-flood-decree with the **specific divine-actors** named — An and Enlil; the senior-divine-pair whose command-spoken cannot be reversed. The verb *šu bal* 'to overturn / reverse' + negative *nu-zu* 'unknown / not-existing' is parallel to the *šu gi4-gi4 nu-ĝal2* of C:24.
lines.cuneiform: 𒅗 𒅗𒂵 𒀭 𒀭𒂗𒆤𒇲𒅗 𒋗 𒁄𒂊 𒉡𒍪

i18n.en: 'Its kingship, its term (of office), has been [torn out — they have wearied of taking counsel].'

lines.commentary: *nam-lugal-bi bal-bi ba-[bur12 e-ne šag4 kuš2-u3-de3]* — *'Its kingship, its term (of office), has been [torn out — they have wearied of taking counsel]'*. The line announces the **end-of-the-antediluvian-kingship-era**: the kingship that descended from heaven at FLS-WOH-B:6 is now **torn out** (verb *bur12* 'to tear out, remove'); the *bal* 'term-in-office' is over. The gods have **wearied of taking counsel** (*šag4 kuš2* 'to tire the heart / be tired in deliberation') — a poetic-anthropomorphism for the decree-as-final. Cross-corpus to the Sumerian King List's transition-between-kingships and to the post-flood restart-of-kingship at Kish.
lines.cuneiform: 𒉆𒈗𒁉 𒁄𒁉 𒁀𒁍 𒂊𒉈 𒊮 𒊨𒅇𒉈

lines.commentary: *e-ne-eš2 ...* — *'Now ...'*. The Sumerian narrative-deictic *i3-ne-eš2* 'now' opens a new discourse-segment; the continuation is bracketed. The line likely begins a transitional-or-imperative-instruction following the kingship-revocation announcement.

i18n.en: 'What […]'

lines.commentary: *a-na MU-MU ...* — *'What ...'*. The Sumerian interrogative *a-na* 'what' opens a question; the continuation (with the unparsed *MU-MU*) is bracketed.

i18n.en: [Approximately 38 lines missing.]
All the destructive storms and gale-winds, every one of them, stood together as one.

lines.commentary: ***im-ḫul-im-ḫul ^tum9si-si-ig du3-a-bi teš2-bi i3-sug2-ge-eš* — *All the destructive storms and gale-winds, every one of them, stood together as one***. The opening of segment D — the **actualization** of the flood-storm decreed in segment C. The Sumerian *im-ḫul* (Akkadian-loanword *imḫullu*) is the foundational Mesopotamian destructive-wind vocabulary (covered by the new central entry `im-hul-imhullu-destructive-storm-wind-mesopotamian-storm-vocabulary-cross-corpus`); cross-corpus to Enuma Elish IV.96 (Marduk's evil-wind weapon) and the Hebrew *ruach ra'ah*. The paired *si-si-ig* gale-wind (covered by the overlay entry `si-si-ig-gale-wind-storm-vocabulary`) escalates. The reduplication-and-pairing produces a comprehensive **all-storm-and-wind-vocabulary-mobilized** image: the entirety of the storm-weather-system is mobilized as a single agent.

i18n.en: The flood swept over the cult-centres.

lines.commentary: *a-ma-ru ugu kab dug4-ga ba-an-da-ab-ur3-e* — *the flood swept over the cult-centres*. The line is the **actualization** of the flood-announcement at FLS-WOH-C:22 (*a-ma-ru ugu kab dug4-ga ba-ur3* — *a flood will sweep over the cult-centres*). The verbatim-recurrence of the announcement-and-execution couplet is the Sumerian narrative's prophecy-fulfillment-marker.

i18n.en: For seven days and seven nights —

lines.commentary: ***ud 7-am3 ĝi6 7-am3* — *For seven days and seven nights***. **THE SEVEN-DAY FLOOD** — the canonical Mesopotamian flood-duration formula. Covered by the new central entry `seven-day-flood-vs-forty-day-flood-duration-tradition-cross-corpus`. Cross-corpus Atrahasis III.iv.24-25 (*seven days seven nights*); Gilgamesh XI.128 (*six days and seven nights* — the variant); contrast Hebrew Gen 7:12 (*forty days and forty nights*). The Mesopotamian-7 → Hebrew-40 transformation is **one of the most-cited cross-corpus Mesopotamian-Hebrew flood-tradition diagnostics** — the Hebrew tradition multiplies the Mesopotamian seven by approximately six to yield the typologically-intensified forty.

i18n.en: after the flood had swept over the Land,

lines.commentary: *a-ma-ru kalam-ma ba-ur3-ra-ta* — *after the flood had swept over the Land*. The temporal-subordinate clause introduces the **post-storm-pericope** at D:5-11. The *kalam* 'the Land' is the Sumerian collective-territorial-identity (covered by the existing central entry `kalam-ka-na-ag-the-land-cross-corpus`).

i18n.en: and the great boat had been tossed by the destructive storms on the great waters,

lines.commentary: ***^ĝišma2 gur4-gur4 a gal-la im-ḫul tuku4-tuku4-a-ta* — *and the great boat had been tossed by the destructive storms on the great waters***. The Sumerian *ma2 gur4-gur4* — *the great boat / the rounded boat* — is Ziusudra's vessel. Covered by the new central entry `ma-gur-eleppu-tevah-flood-vessel-cross-corpus` — three-way sibling-cluster with the Akkadian *eleppu* (Atrahasis, Gilgamesh XI) and the Hebrew *tevah* (Gen 6:14-16, Exod 2:3). The verb *tuku4* 'to shake / toss' captures the boat's storm-tossed motion on the great-waters.

i18n.en: Utu came forth, casting his light over heaven and earth.

lines.commentary: ***^dutu i-im-ma-ra-e3 an ki-a ud ĝa2-ĝa2* — *Utu came forth, casting his light over heaven and earth***. The **post-storm-sunrise**: Utu (Sumerian sun-god; Akkadian Šamaš; covered by the new central entry `utu-shamash-sun-god-justice-divinity-cross-corpus`) emerges after the seven-day storm. Cross-corpus Gilgamesh XI.131-134 (the storm subsides; the day brightens); Hebrew Gen 8:1 (*va-yaaver Elohim ruach al ha-aretz va-yashoku ha-mayim* — *Elohim caused a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters abated*).
lines.cuneiform: 𒀭𒌓 𒄿𒅎𒈠𒊏𒌓𒁺 𒀭 𒆠𒀀 𒌓 𒂷𒂷

i18n.en: Ziusudra cut an opening in the great boat.

lines.commentary: ***zi-ud-su3-ra2 ^ĝišma2 gur4-gur4 ab-BUR2 mu-un-da-buru3* — *Ziusudra cut an opening in the great boat***. The **boat-window / aperture** trope. The Sumerian *ab-BUR2* (covered by the new central entry `ab-bur-aptu-chalon-ha-tevah-flood-boat-window-cross-corpus`) sits in three-way sibling-cluster with the Akkadian *aptu* (Gilgamesh XI.135-136 — *aptam upattī-ma ūru iqtul ina pānīya* — *I opened the window, and light fell upon my face*) and the Hebrew *chalon ha-tevah* (Gen 8:6 — *va-yiftach Noach et chalon ha-tevah*). The flood-survivor-opens-aperture trope is one of the most-cited cross-corpus diagnostics for the Mesopotamian-Hebrew flood-tradition.

i18n.en: The young hero Utu brought his light into the great boat.

lines.commentary: *šul ^dutu ĝiš-nu11-ni-da ^ĝišma2 gur4-gur4-še3 ba-an-kur9-re-en* — *The young hero Utu brought his light into the great boat*. Utu's light enters through the just-cut aperture (D:7); the Sumerian *ĝiš-nu11* 'light' is the technical-luminescence vocabulary. The line is the symmetric-counterpart to Gilgamesh XI.135-136 (*ūru iqtul ina pānīya* — *light fell upon my face*).

i18n.en: Ziusudra the king

lines.commentary: *zi-ud-su3-ra2 lugal-am3* — *Ziusudra the king*. The Sumerian *lugal* 'king' title continues from C:11; here functions as the subject-of-the-following-line (D:10), with the line-break used for emphatic-position.

i18n.en: prostrated himself before Utu, rubbing his nose to the ground.

lines.commentary: ***igi ^dutu-še3 giri17 ki su-ub ba-gub* — *prostrated himself before Utu, rubbing his nose to the ground***. The full-body **prostration gesture** — Sumerian *giri17 ki su-ub* (literally 'rubbing the nose to the ground'); cross-corpus the Akkadian *appa labānu* and the Hebrew *shachah apayim artzah*. Covered by the new central entry `giri-ki-su-ub-appa-labanu-prostration-gesture-cross-corpus`. The first post-flood-prostration (the second is before An and Enlil at FLS-WOH-E:5). Ziusudra's prostration before Utu is the **thanksgiving-for-the-post-storm-sunrise** moment — Utu the sun-god (and divinity-of-justice) is the first deity acknowledged after the storm.
lines.cuneiform: 𒅆 𒀭𒌓𒂠 𒅗 𒆠 𒋢𒌒 𒁀𒁺

i18n.en: The king slaughtered an ox and offered up sheep in abundance.

lines.commentary: ***lugal-e gud im-ma-ab-gaz-e udu im-ma-ab-šar2-re* — *The king slaughtered an ox and offered up sheep in abundance***. The **post-flood thanksgiving-sacrifice** — one of the most-cited cross-corpus Mesopotamian-Hebrew flood-tradition parallels. Covered by the new central entry `post-flood-thanksgiving-sacrifice-trope-cross-corpus`. Cross-corpus Atrahasis III.v (Atrahasis's sacrifice; the gods crowd around the smoke *like flies*); Gilgamesh XI.155-160 (Utnapishtim's sacrifice; the gods smell *erīša ṭāba* 'the sweet savor'); Hebrew Gen 8:20-21 (Noah builds an altar; YHWH smells *reiach ha-nichoach* 'the sweet savor'). The Hebrew *reiach ha-nichoach* and the Akkadian *erīša ṭāba* are **lexical-and-semantic cognates** — one of the most-direct Mesopotamian-Hebrew lexical-parallels in the flood-tradition.

i18n.en: […] a great horn […] (made) pure […]

lines.commentary: *[...] X si gal [...] sikil-la-da* — *[...] a great horn [...] (made) pure [...]*. The line is heavily-fragmented; the preserved *si gal* 'great horn' and *sikil-la-da* 'in purity / purified' indicate residual sacrifice-and-purification vocabulary continuing from the D:11 thanksgiving-sacrifice scene.

i18n.en: […] was allotted to him […]

lines.commentary: *[...] X mu-un-na-X-X-ba* — *[...] was allotted to him [...]*. The preserved verb *ba* 'to allot / divide / distribute' suggests a continuing-allocation-and-allotment scene; the addressee (*-na-* '-to-him-') is implied to be Ziusudra. Unrecoverable beyond the verbal-sense.
Reduced to bare brackets — *[...]*. Fully-lacuna.

i18n.en: […] he filled.

lines.commentary: *[...] bi2-in-si* — *[...] he filled*. The preserved verb *si* 'to fill / fill up' indicates a residual filling-action; the object is unrecoverable.

i18n.en: […] paired […]

lines.commentary: *[...] X tab-ba* — *[...] paired [...]*. The preserved verb *tab* 'to be parallel / paired' indicates a pairing-action — possibly the pairs-of-animals continuation (Gen 7:2-3 has Noah load the pairs into the ark; the Mesopotamian flood-tradition's pair-of-animals motif may be reflected here).
*[...] A X* — fully-lacuna with only residual cuneiform-sign-traces. Unrecoverable.

lines.translit: zi an-na zi ki-a i3-pad3-de3-en-ze2-en za-zu-da ḫe2-em-da-la2

i18n.en: 'You (gods) have sworn by the life of heaven and the life of earth — you yourselves should be bound by it.'

lines.commentary: ***zi an-na zi ki-a i3-pad3-de3-en-ze2-en za-zu-da ḫe2-em-da-la2* — *'You (gods) have sworn by the life of heaven and the life of earth — you yourselves should be bound by it'***. **THE OATH-BY-LIFE-OF-HEAVEN-AND-LIFE-OF-EARTH FORMULA** — the foundational Mesopotamian oath-formula. The Sumerian *zi an-na zi ki-a* deploys the *zi* life-breath keyword (covered by the existing central entry `zi-sumerian-breath-of-life-cross-corpus`) to invoke the **animating-vitality of heaven and earth** as the binding-substance of the oath. Covered by the new central entry `zi-an-na-zi-ki-a-nish-ilim-oath-by-life-of-heaven-and-earth-cross-corpus`. The cluster spans three-way Sumerian-Akkadian-Hebrew: Sumerian *zi an-na zi ki-a* ↔ Akkadian *nīš ilī* / *nīš šamê u erṣetim* ↔ Hebrew *chay YHWH* (1 Sam 14:39, Jer 4:2; covered by the existing central entry `chei-x-oath-by-the-life-formula`). Reception-history extends through Matt 5:34-35 (Jesus' prohibition of swearing-by-heaven-or-earth).
lines.cuneiform: 𒍣 𒀭𒈾 𒍣 𒆠𒀀 𒉌𒅆𒊒𒉈𒂗𒍢𒂗 𒍝𒍪𒁕 𒅎𒁕𒇲

lines.translit: an ^den-lil2 zi an-na zi ki-a i3-pad3-de3-ze2-en za-da-ne-ne im-da-la2

i18n.en: An and Enlil swore by the life of heaven and the life of earth, and were bound by it themselves.

lines.commentary: *an ^den-lil2 zi an-na zi ki-a i3-pad3-de3-ze2-en za-da-ne-ne im-da-la2* — *An and Enlil swore by the life of heaven and the life of earth, and were bound by it themselves*. The **reciprocal-binding** of the divine assembly by their own oath. An and Enlil — the senior pair who decreed the flood (FLS-WOH-C:25) — are now bound by their oath. The narrative-effect is the **reversal-of-the-flood-decree-irrevocability** at the divine-self-binding level: the gods who decreed the flood now swear-themselves-into-restraint regarding any repetition.
lines.cuneiform: 𒀭 𒀭𒂗𒆤 𒍣 𒀭𒈾 𒍣 𒆠𒀀 𒉌𒅆𒊒𒉈𒍢𒂗 𒍝𒁕𒉈𒉈 𒅎𒁕𒇲

i18n.en: The small animals that come up from the earth came forth.

lines.commentary: *niĝ2-gilim-ma ki-ta ed3-de3 im-ma-ra-ed3-de3* — *The small animals that come up from the earth came forth*. The line names the **post-flood-emergence of the small-animals** — paralleling the creation-of-animals at FLS-WOH-A:13-14 (where the small-animals multiplied from the ground in every place). The cyclical pattern: animals are fashioned from the ground (A:13) → destroyed in the flood → re-emerge from the ground (E:3). The continuity-through-the-flood is the diagnostic of Ziusudra's preservation-mission (covered at FLS-WOH-E:10 by the new central entry `preservation-of-the-seed-of-humankind-and-animals-flood-aitia-cross-corpus`).

i18n.en: Ziusudra the king

lines.commentary: *zi-ud-su3-ra2 lugal-am3* — *Ziusudra the king*. The Sumerian *lugal* 'king' title continues from D:9 and C:11; here functions as the subject-of-the-following-line (E:5), with the line-break for emphatic-position. The same enjambment-construction recurs at FLS-WOH-E:9.

lines.translit: igi an ^den-lil2-la2-še3 giri17 ki su-ub ba-/gub^!\

i18n.en: prostrated himself before An and Enlil, rubbing his nose to the ground.

lines.commentary: *igi an ^den-lil2-la2-še3 giri17 ki su-ub ba-/gub^!\* — *prostrated himself before An and Enlil, rubbing his nose to the ground*. The **second post-flood-prostration** (the first was before Utu at FLS-WOH-D:10). Now before An and Enlil — the senior pair of the divine quartet — preceding the apotheosis-grant of FLS-WOH-E:6-8. The prostration-gesture is covered by the new central entry `giri-ki-su-ub-appa-labanu-prostration-gesture-cross-corpus`; the same idiom across Sumerian-Akkadian-Hebrew (Hebrew *shachah apayim artzah*).
lines.cuneiform: 𒅆 𒀭 𒀭𒂗𒆤𒇲𒂠 𒅗 𒆠 𒋢𒌒 𒁀

i18n.en: An and Enlil cherished Ziusudra and [spoke …] to him.

lines.commentary: *an ^den-lil2 zi-ud-su3-ra2 mi2-e-/eš2^?\ [...-dug4-...]* — *An and Enlil cherished Ziusudra and [spoke ...] to him*. The Sumerian *mi2 dug4* (literally 'to speak loving-care') is the technical-idiom for **divine-favor / cherishing**. The line is the transition into the apotheosis-grant at FLS-WOH-E:7-8.

i18n.en: Life like (that of) a god they gave him.

lines.commentary: ***til3 diĝir-gin7 mu-un-na-šum2-mu* — *Life like (that of) a god they gave him***. The **apotheosis-grant**. Covered by the new central entry `til-digir-gin-kima-ilani-apotheosis-of-flood-survivor-cross-corpus`. The Sumerian *til3 diĝir-gin7* sits in cross-corpus sibling-cluster with the Akkadian *kīma ilāni* (Gilgamesh XI.193-196 — *let Utnapishtim and his wife become like the gods*); the Hebrew structural-parallel is the Hanokh-translation (Gen 5:24 — *for the Elohim took him*) and the Eliyahu-whirlwind-ascent (2 Kgs 2:11); cross-references to the existing central entry `noach-vayithallech` (the *Noah walked with the Elohim* parallel-construction). The Hebrew Bible has **no flood-survivor apotheosis** — Noah dies a natural death (Gen 9:29); the Mesopotamian apotheosis is conspicuously absent at the Hebrew flood-narrative.

i18n.en: Eternal breath of life like (that of) a god they brought down for him.

lines.commentary: ***zi da-ri2 diĝir-gin7 mu-un--ab-ed3-de3* — *Eternal breath of life like (that of) a god they brought down for him***. The line **doubles the apotheosis-grant** with the explicit *zi da-ri2* 'eternal life-breath' qualifier (covered by the new central entry `zi-da-ri-balatu-daru-eternal-life-cross-corpus`). The Sumerian *da-ri2* 'eternal' is the source of the Akkadian-loanword *dārû*; the Akkadian *balāṭu dārû* 'eternal life' is the direct cognate-parallel. Hebrew comparanda: *chayei olam* (Dan 12:2 — the Hebrew Bible's most-explicit eternal-life formula) and *brit olam* 'everlasting covenant' (the *olam* eternal-modifier in covenantal contexts; covered by the existing central entry `brit-olam`).

i18n.en: In those days Ziusudra the king,

lines.commentary: *ud-ba zi-ud-su3-ra2 lugal-am3* — *In those days Ziusudra the king,*. The temporal-deictic *ud-ba* 'in those days' opens the closing-narrative-frame; the enjambment continues to E:10-11 (the *for-preserving / they settled him* aitia-and-destination).

lines.translit: mu niĝ2-gilim-ma numun nam-lu2-ulu3 uru3 ak

i18n.en: for preserving the small animals and the seed of humankind —

lines.commentary: ***mu niĝ2-gilim-ma numun nam-lu2-ulu3 uru3 ak* — *for preserving the small animals and the seed of humankind***. The **explicit aitia for Ziusudra's apotheosis**: he is rewarded *because* he preserved both the small-animals and the seed-of-humankind through the flood. Covered by the new central entry `preservation-of-the-seed-of-humankind-and-animals-flood-aitia-cross-corpus`. Cross-corpus Atrahasis III.vi (the *zēr napišti* preservation); Gilgamesh XI.193-195 (Utnapishtim's preservation-merit); Hebrew Gen 7:3 (*l-chayyot zera al penei kol ha-aretz* — *to keep seed alive on the face of all the earth*) and Gen 9:1-7 (the post-flood-blessing; covered by the existing central entry `peru-urevu-postflood`). The Mesopotamian reward-form is **apotheosis-of-the-survivor** (immortality-grant); the Hebrew reward-form is **fertility-blessing-of-the-descendants** (mortal-blessing). The transformation is one of the most-significant Mesopotamian-Hebrew flood-tradition divergences.

lines.translit: kur-bal kur dilmun-na ki ^dutu e3-še3 mu-un-til3-eš

i18n.en: they settled him in an overseas country, in the land of Dilmun, the place where Utu rises.

lines.commentary: ***kur-bal kur dilmun-na ki ^dutu e3-še3 mu-un-til3-eš* — *they settled him in an overseas country, in the land of Dilmun, the place where Utu rises***. **DILMUN — the eastern paradise**. Covered by the new central entry `dilmun-eastern-paradise-cross-corpus`. Dilmun is identified historically with **modern Bahrain** and the eastern Persian Gulf region; archaeologically attested from the third millennium. The Sumerian *kur dilmun-na* + *ki ^dutu e3-še3* (*the place where Utu rises*) is the **eastern-cosmographic-orientation**. Cross-corpus: Akkadian Gilgamesh XI.205-206 (Utnapishtim is settled *ina rūqi ina pî nārāti* 'in the far-distance, at the mouth of the rivers'); Hebrew Gen 2:8 (*va-yitta YHWH Elohim gan b-Eden mi-qedem* — *YHWH planted a garden in Eden, in the east*; covered by the existing central entry `gan-be-eden`). The Sumerian Enki-and-Ninhursag composition (ETCSL 1.1.1 — the *Dilmun-paradise-text*) is the most-developed Sumerian Eden-comparandum. The entry's rationale documents explicit operational disavowals against the ancient-astronaut interpretive overlays (Sitchin-corpus *Dilmun-as-spaceport* readings).
lines.cuneiform: 𒆳𒁄 𒆳 𒉌𒌇𒈾 𒆠 𒀭𒌓 𒌓𒁺𒂠 𒈬𒌦𒋾𒌍

i18n.en: 'You, […] there they shall live […]'

lines.commentary: *za-e^? X [...] /BA\ X-bi til3-eš X* — *'You, [...] there they shall live [...]'*. The preserved fragments contain the 2sg-pronoun *za-e* 'you' and the verb *til3-eš* 'they shall live / let them live'. The line is plausibly the closing-direct-address to Ziusudra or to the audience — possibly the opening of a doxological-closing-formula (cf. the Sumerian *za-mi* doxological tradition covered by the existing central entry `za-mi-doxological-praise-formula-sumerian-cross-corpus`). The composition's expected closing-doxology is mostly-lost in the lacuna.
